correctness.rationale: For rational gamma=q/p in (0,1) and critical nu=1/(1+gamma), direct substitution into the piecewise map gives the exact (not limiting) return P_M,lambda(z)=epsilon z+nu*(lambda^(-gamma)-epsilon)*((1-z)/(1-nu))^gamma, epsilon=nu^M. P(z)-z decreases strictly and changes sign at z=nu,1 for lambda in (nu^(1/gamma),1), so a unique fixed point yields exactly one nonlinear and M-1 strict linear visits, hence primitive period M. Eliminating the amplitude with the fixed-point equation yields multiplier epsilon-gamma(1-epsilon)z/(1-z); its unique -1 crossing occurs at z*=(1+epsilon)/(1+gamma+(1-gamma)epsilon), defining lambda*. Taylor expansion gives lambda*=1-4nu^(M+1)+O(nu^(2M)) and relative physical-mu window width =4gamma nu/(1-gamma)*nu^M+O(nu^(2M)). The return Schwarzian at flip is eventually strictly positive and transverse crossing gives a repelling local doubled-return orbit on stable side (subcritical flip). Independent high-precision parameter/root checks for gamma=1/2,1/3,2/5 and M=8,20,50 corroborate exact equations and limiting ratios; no extrapolation of numerical tests.
residual_risks: Rational gamma in (0,1), critical nu=1/(1+gamma), M sufficiently large; upper grazing endpoint excluded.
